summative_rubric.title: G3 Fencing the Farm — Summative Rubric
summative_rubric.purpose: Used during and after Lesson 5 to score against E2 expectations.

rows.expectation_text: use appropriate units of length to estimate, measure, and compare the perimeters of polygons and curved shapes, and construct polygons with a given perimeter

levels.descriptor: Cannot find perimeter. Adds wrong sides.
Finds perimeter with prompts.
Independently measures perimeter and constructs polygons.
Compares perimeters across shapes and explains.

rows.expectation_text: compare the areas of two-dimensional shapes by matching, covering, or decomposing and recomposing the shapes, and demonstrate that different shapes can have the same area

levels.descriptor: Confuses area with perimeter.
Compares areas with prompts.
Independently compares areas by covering or decomposing.
Identifies different shapes with the same area.

rows.expectation_text: use square centimetres (cm2) and square metres (m2) to estimate, measure, and compare the areas of various two-dimensional shapes, including those with curved sides

levels.descriptor: Cannot use cm². Wrong unit choice.
Counts cm² with prompts.
Independently counts cm² and picks cm² or m² appropriately.
Estimates curved-shape area with whole + half squares.

rows.expectation_text: use non-standard units appropriately to estimate, measure, and compare capacity, and explain the effect that overfilling or underfilling, and gaps between units, have on accuracy

levels.descriptor: Cannot compare capacity.
Compares with prompts.
Independently measures and compares capacity with non-standard units.
Explains overfill/underfill effects.

rows.expectation_text: use analog and digital clocks and timers to tell time in hours, minutes, and seconds

levels.descriptor: Confuses hour and minute hands.
Reads analog or digital clock with prompts.
Independently reads analog and digital clocks.
Reads to seconds; converts hours-minutes-seconds.

rows.expectation_text: explain the relationships between millimetres, centimetres, metres, and kilometres as metric units of length, and use benchmarks for these units to estimate lengths

levels.descriptor: Cannot pick the right unit for the size.
Picks unit with prompts and benchmarks.
Independently picks mm/cm/m/km using benchmarks.
Converts between units (10 mm = 1 cm; 100 cm = 1 m).

rows.expectation_text: compare, estimate, and measure the mass of various objects, using a pan balance and non-standard units

levels.descriptor: Cannot read pan balance.
Reads heavier or lighter with prompts.
Independently compares mass using a pan balance.
Estimates mass before measuring.

rows.expectation_text: use various units of different sizes to measure the same attribute of a given item, and demonstrate that even though using different-sized units produces a different count, the size of the attribute remains the same

levels.descriptor: Thinks different counts mean different attribute.
Recognizes same-attribute with prompts.
Independently shows same attribute under different units.
Articulates inverse relation: bigger unit, fewer counts.

rows.expectation_text: use appropriate non-standard units to measure area, and explain the effect that gaps and overlaps have on accuracy

levels.descriptor: Tiles with gaps or overlaps without noticing.
Tiles edge-to-edge with prompts.
Independently tiles edge-to-edge and explains gaps/overlaps.
Quantifies gap/overlap error.

summative_task_script.title: Big Farm Capstone — Summative Administration Guide
summative_task_script.purpose: Ties Lesson 5 capstone, the 4 stations, and the rubric together.
administration_steps: Before: photocopy templates, print rubric, ready Junior Measurer certificates.
Stations 1-4 (6 min each): PERIMETER, AREA, CAPACITY/MASS, TIME.
Station 1 PERIMETER: measure 2 polygons. Evidence E2.1.
Station 2 AREA: count cm² for 2 shapes. Evidence E2.7, E2.9.
Station 3 CAPACITY/MASS: compare 2 cards. Evidence E2.3, E2.4.
Station 4 TIME: read 4 clocks. Evidence E2.6.
summative_task_script.scoring_guidance: Use the Capstone Template as primary evidence. Level 3 = grade-level.
